item.title: HUB75 Power Connections
item.description:
A prototype concept for distributing 5 V power from one supply to the HUB75 LED matrix panels.

Proposed concept

The prototype is deliberately simple:

  • 1 × removable 20 A input for the main 5 V supply;
  • 2 × 4-pole barrier-strip terminals for the HUB75 panel outputs;
  • 1 × additional 2-pole 10 A screw terminal for PCB / auxiliary 5 V;
  • all mounted on a 4 × 6 cm double-sided experiment PCB.

The two 4-pole barrier strips provide eight screw positions in total. Five positions are intended for the five HUB75 panel feeds, leaving three spare positions.

item.title: Useful Git Commands
item.description:
Practical commands for everyday Git work. Steps that depend on GitHub are explicitly labelled.

Clone a repository

Open the terminal in Visual Studio Code and choose the parent directory before cloning:

cd C:\projects
git clone <repository-url>

GitHub example: include the account name in the HTTPS URL when you work with multiple GitHub accounts:

git clone https://username@github.com/username/repository-name.git

Open the checkout in Visual Studio Code and inspect the configured remote:

cd repository-name
code .
git remote -v

The username in the URL identifies the intended account; authentication is handled separately, normally by Git Credential Manager.

item.title: About
item.description:
About brainboxemb

brainboxemb grew from the idea of a brainbox: a place to capture, structure and keep technical ideas, references and lessons that would otherwise live only in my head. The emb part reflects one of my main interests: embedded electronics and software.

That includes microcontrollers, displays, protocols, Raspberry Pi, hardware/software integration and the tooling around them. From there, the site naturally branches into 3D printing, CAD, workshop and DIY projects, tools, AI and other technical experiments.

item.title: AI-assisted content
item.description:
Parts of this site are created, edited or researched with AI assistance.

AI is used as a practical tool for drafting, restructuring notes, summarising supplied references, researching technical details and maintaining the site. The resulting content is reviewed during normal use of the site, but it may still contain errors, outdated information, incomplete interpretations or incorrect conclusions.

For technical details that matter for safety, compatibility, purchasing decisions or implementation, verify the information against the original manufacturer, project, standards documentation or other primary source.
